root_causes.description: An HTTP-boundary abort on the product-catalog leaf (called by recommendation and frontend) prevents its requests from completing normally, so callers block until the 10s deadline and client-facing requests error out. product-catalog itself emits no completed/errored server span, so its own error and latency metrics remain normal — the classic abort-at-HTTP-boundary signature.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 and no completed server spans for product-catalog during the window
evidence.expected_baseline: product-catalog normally emits a steady stream of successful server spans; an aborted HTTP boundary produces no completed/errored span

evidence.observed_value: recommendation p99=10000 ms flat at the 10s deadline throughout the window
evidence.expected_baseline: recommendation server p99 well below 1s; a flat 10s indicates the caller is blocking on an unresponsive downstream (product-catalog)

evidence.observed_value: frontend-proxy error_rate=0.224, flagd=0.010, frontend=0.007, checkout=0.000, cart/payment=0.000
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend-proxy client/server error rate near 0; 0.224 is the dominant error signal for this incident
browse/recommendation traces normally complete in tens of ms; 15s durations reflect blocked downstream calls

root_causes.description: recommendation's server p99 sits flat at 10000 ms across the entire window, indicating its calls (or its dependency product-catalog) stall to the 10s deadline. Could itself be the injected latency service rather than merely a victim of product-catalog.

evidence.expected_baseline: recommendation server p99 should be sub-second
recommendation-dependent browse traces expected in tens of ms

root_causes.description: The outer frontend/frontend-proxy tier shows the highest observable error rate (0.224), consistent with upstream requests failing/timing out because a downstream (product-catalog/recommendation) never returns. Alternative if the abort was injected at the frontend edge rather than the catalog leaf.

evidence.expected_baseline: expected near-zero client/server error rate at the edge
frontend-proxy error logs expected if the edge itself were faulting; absence weakens this hypothesis

remediation_steps: Disable/roll back the http_abort fault injection on product-catalog (the flagd flag controlling the product-catalog HTTP abort) to restore normal responses.
Restart the product-catalog deployment pods to clear any stuck/aborted connection state.
Verify recommendation server p99 latency returns below ~1s and frontend-proxy error rate drops back toward 0 after the rollback.
If metrics do not recover, re-check recommendation and frontend for the injected latency/abort fault in the same window.
